_what: Which surface a long operation opens. Two populations, both enforced by progress-surface.test.ts. 'directProgress' is every vscode.window.withProgress outside the five modules that own the surfaces — each entry says why it still opens its own notification instead of going through withOperationProgress, and the list may only shrink. 'blockingDialogs' is every modal:true dialog — each entry names the decision it gates, because a blocking dialog is for a choice made BEFORE work starts and for nothing else.

directProgress.src/commands/commandManager.ts:408: Adobe sign-in, started from the palette, a dashboard button and a wizard step. It is not an operation with stages — one title, one spinner, nothing to report — and the router would have nothing to route.
directProgress.src/commands/migrateStorefrontNames.ts:1: A one-off maintenance command run from the palette. R2 already says one notification, which is what this opens; nothing else narrates it.
directProgress.src/commands/repairSiteConfiguration.ts:: The republish half of the same palette command. Moving it alone would split one command across two surfaces.
Palette maintenance command, reads the site's configuration. One notification is the right surface; it predates the router.
directProgress.src/core/utils/browserUtils.ts:52: Covers the second or two Chrome takes to start a private window. There is no operation to narrate and nothing can fail slowly. The two screens that open a live site used to write this out separately; they now call it here.
directProgress.src/features/authentication/handlers/del: Reports stages through stageLine into its own notification. A candidate for the router — it has stages and a screen behind it — and the reason it has not moved is that its teardown reports a step/total shape the ReportStage signature takes differently.
directProgress.src/features/authentication/services/ens: Telegraphs the browser launch during a forced sign-in. Not an operation: the work is in the browser, and the notification exists so the delay is not silent.
directProgress.src/features/dashboard/commands/configur: Author-mode switch from the Configure screen. Short, single-step; R5 (a busy state on the control) would be the better answer, which is a UI change, not a routing one.
directProgress.src/features/eds/commands/cleanupDaLiveS: The deletion itself, from the palette. R2 says one notification; this is it.
Palette command, reading the site list before anything is chosen. This is the load, not the work.
directProgress.src/features/eds/commands/manageGitHubRe: The repository deletion itself, from the palette. One notification is the right surface.
Palette command, loading the repository list before anything is chosen.
directProgress.src/features/eds/handlers/daLive/daLiveA: Verifies credentials the SC has just pasted, inside the prompt that asked for them. The prompt is the surface; this covers the check.
directProgress.src/features/project-creation/services/a: Runs when a VS Code setting changes, so there is no screen and no agent — a notification is the only surface available.
directProgress.src/commands/commandManager.ts:467: GitHub sign-in from the palette: one notification while the browser flow completes, the same shape as the Adobe sign-in above it (develop, merged 2026-09-24).

blockingDialogs.src/features/dashboard/handlers/appBuild: Gates: create a PUBLIC GitHub repository and push the app to it? Only when no screen modal is asking; from the card the same yes is the modal's Create button.
blockingDialogs.src/commands/ResetAiOnboardingCommand.ts: Gates: reset the AI onboarding surface? Destructive and asked once, before anything runs.
blockingDialogs.src/commands/ResetAllCommand.ts:28: Gates: delete all Demo Builder data and state? The most destructive thing the extension offers.
blockingDialogs.src/commands/migrateStorefrontNames.ts:1: Gates: rename these storefronts? The detail lists exactly which ones, so the SC answers with the list in front of them.
blockingDialogs.src/core/base/baseCommand.ts:258: The generic confirm every command asks through. It gates whatever its caller is about to do; the callers are where the decision is named.
blockingDialogs.src/core/vscode/operationPrompt.ts:136: Gates: sign in (or answer another question the work needs) before an agent's call can go on. Modal like the agent's consent dialogs, so a question an agent asks is never a corner notification (owner, 2026-09-21).
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/commands/cleanupDaLiveS: Gates: delete these DA.live sites? Named in the detail: the pages come off the live site and the content does not come back.
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/commands/manageGitHubRe: Gates: delete these GitHub repositories? Named in the detail, and they do not come back.
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/handlers/storefrontSetu: Gates: cancel setup, knowing the GitHub repo and DA.live content created so far will be deleted? The cost of stopping is not obvious without asking.
blockingDialogs.src/features/lifecycle/services/projectR: Gates: delete the components and reinstall them from scratch? Configuration and integrations survive, the rest does not.
blockingDialogs.src/features/ai/server/agentOperationNot: Gates: let the agent run this tool? A cloud write an agent proposes is confirmed by a person before it happens.
blockingDialogs.src/features/project-creation/handlers/e: Gates: an Edit that changes the package resets the storefront to it. Its code and content are replaced; asked before anything in the Edit runs (PL-75).
Gates: an Edit that unticks integrations undeploys them. Asked by name, before anything in the Edit runs (PL-75).
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/services/reset/edsReset: Gates: reset this storefront to the template and re-copy demo content? Hand edits are lost. Not asked within an Edit, which asks its own version before anything runs.
blockingDialogs.src/features/data-installer/handlers/pri: Gates: share the project's private library pack before its file goes out, since a teammate cannot read it otherwise (owner, 2026-10-30). Asked once per export; Export Anyway (and Esc) exports without sharing.
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/services/reset/edsReset: Gates: also clear what the demo's store holds that Demo Builder did not install, and close its orders (through the ERP integration where one serves the store, then refreshing its ERP), to leave its store empty (datapack-engine step 10). Names the store and says it cannot be undone; asked only after Remove Datapack, or with no datapack, and only when there is something to clear. Esc keeps everything.

Gates: also remove the datapack this project imported from the Commerce instance, which takes several minutes and is not needed for a storefront reset (or, in an Edit that changes the datapack, before the new pack is imported)? A separate, costlier choice inside the same flow.
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/handlers/forgetAddedDem: Gates: take an added demo's card off the Welcome step — and, for a demo added from a zip, whether the repository made from it goes too. Modal because the detail names what stays and what goes before the click (develop, merged 2026-09-24).
Gates: delete the repository made from the zip file. Irreversible, so it is asked on its own, after the first choice, and only when that choice included it (develop, merged 2026-09-24).
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/services/reset/edsReset: Gates: keep the site's current content when the demo's source pages cannot be reached — the SC chooses between resetting code only and an empty site. A decision only they can make, asked before the reset starts (develop, merged 2026-09-24).
blockingDialogs.src/core/build/buildStampUi.ts:72: Not a decision: shows which build of Demo Builder is running. Modal on purpose, because it is read when someone is unsure which build they have, and a toast that disappears is too easy to miss.
blockingDialogs.src/features/authentication/handlers/del: Gates: permanently delete an Adobe I/O project and its event registrations and providers. Cannot be undone.
blockingDialogs.src/features/dashboard/handlers/appBuild: Gates: delete from GitHub the repository Demo Builder created when an app was saved to one. Cannot be undone. Skipped only for an agent that sends confirm: true after asking the user (delete_app_github_repo).
blockingDialogs.src/features/dashboard/handlers/destinat: Gates: move the project to another Adobe project, which removes each integration with a workspace of its own from the old one (uninstalled from Commerce, workspace deleted). An Edit asks this before anything runs.
blockingDialogs.src/features/projects-dashboard/services: Gates: delete a project's files and configuration from this computer. Cannot be undone.
blockingDialogs.src/features/project-creation/commands/c: Gates: throw away the changes made in this Edit and open project configuration? Asked only when the Edit has changes; leaving for Configure would discard them.
blockingDialogs.src/features/dashboard/handlers/statusHa: Gates: sign in to Adobe now, which opens the browser? Asked once per expiry when the dashboard finds the sign-in expired; a no opens nothing (owner, 2026-10-17).
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/handlers/daLive/daLiveA: Gates: start a DA.live sign-in the SC asked for, by getting a token from da.live or carrying on with one already copied. A modal so it sits centred while they are in the browser (owner, 2026-10-31).
Gates: read the clipboard once the SC has copied their DA.live token in the browser. Still there, centred, when they come back.
blockingDialogs.src/features/eds/handlers/daLive/daLiveS: Gates: sign in to DA.live again, now that signing in to Adobe again signed the SC out of it. Never awaited, so the work it interrupted carries on behind it (owner, 2026-10-31).
